requirements.title: Construct execution establishes selector-to-associate-name association
requirements.definition: Execution of SELECT RANK or SELECT TYPE establishes association between the selector and associate name. Execution of ASSOCIATE or CHANGE TEAM establishes association between each selector and corresponding associate name.

pending.change-team-association-out-of-scope: Existing owner doc/catalogues/execution_of_a_change_team_construct_11_1_5_2.json covers CHANGE TEAM execution. CHANGE TEAM selector association is team/coarray-dependent here, so it is out of scope by user decision; no single-image two-way runtime plan is registered.

requirements.oracle: S19.5.1.6-001 construct association establishment runtime fixtures: ASSOCIATE, SELECT TYPE, and SELECT RANK fixtures use variable selectors and two-way sentinels: writes through the associate name are visible in the selector and writes through the selector are visible through the associate name. CHANGE TEAM remains pending as coarray/team dependent.
requirements.oracle_limitation: S19.5.1.6-001 construct association establishment fixture boundariess: only the listed single-image exact integer/logical effects are claimed. Coarray/team cases, submodule execution, enum/enumeration syntax, inaccessible-name negative diagnostics, reverse accessibility, DATA ordering restrictions, COMMON/C linkage, IMPORT-only interface-body failure modes, ASYNCHRONOUS/VOLATILE runtime behavior, absent ALLOCATABLE/POINTER attribute inquiries, addresses, diagnostic text, and processor-dependent representations are not asserted and remain pending where appropriate.

requirements.title: Allocatable and pointer selectors in ASSOCIATE or SELECT TYPE have required allocation or association status
requirements.definition: In ASSOCIATE or SELECT TYPE, an allocatable selector shall be allocated and a pointer selector shall be associated.

pending.allocatable-selector-must-be-allocated: Positive control allocates integer allocatable x, sets x=1, ASSOCIATE(a=>x), assigns a=42, and expects x=42; a source-control mutation removes ALLOCATE without claiming a required diagnostic.
pending.pointer-selector-must-be-associated: Positive control pointer p=>target t where t=1 enters ASSOCIATE(a=>p), assigns a=42, and expects t=42; a mutation nullifies p before the construct without claiming a required diagnostic.

requirements.oracle: Source registration only. Future fixtures establish a distinguished non-default state first, then observe only portable single-image properties: exact integer, logical, character, type, rank, bounds, ASSOCIATED inquiry results for defined pointer association status, or required syntax diagnostics owned by a numbered rule. Undefined pointer association status and undefined definition status are never inspected, dereferenced, invoked, compared, or passed to ASSOCIATED as an oracle.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Unnumbered program restrictions are source-control restrictions only. Notes are informative. Coarray, image, team, companion-processor lifetime, volatile-interference, addresses, diagnostic wording, exit status details, and processor-dependent representations are not asserted.

requirements.title: Associate names for allocatable and pointer selectors associate with the selected object or target without selector attributes
requirements.definition: For an allocated allocatable selector, the associate name is associated with the data object and does not have ALLOCATABLE. For an associated pointer selector, the associate name is associated with the target and does not have POINTER.

pending.allocatable-associate-name-no-allocatabl: Allocated integer x=1 enters ASSOCIATE(a=>x); source-control confirms a is used as a scalar data object and allocation inquiry on a is not part of this fixture.
pending.pointer-associate-name-no-pointer: With p=>t, source-control uses a only as the nonpointer associated object; pointer status inquiries are reserved for p and not for associate name a.

requirements.oracle: S19.5.1.6-005 pointer selector target association runtime fixture: with pointer p associated to target t, ASSOCIATE(a=>p) writes through a and observes t, then writes t and observes a, proving the associate name is associated with the pointer target. No runtime inquiry can prove the absence of the POINTER attribute, so that facet remains pending.

requirements.title: Construct association is with the selector object for variables and with a pre-evaluated value for expressions or vector-subscript sections
requirements.definition: For a variable selector other than an array section with a vector subscript, association is with the data object specified by the selector; otherwise association is with the value of the selector expression evaluated before block execution.
requirements.oracle: S19.5.1.6-003 selector object/value association runtime fixtures: variable-selector object association is checked by two-way ASSOCIATE writes. Expression and vector-subscript selectors are checked as pre-evaluated values: changing the contributing variables or selected array elements inside the block does not change the associate-name values.

requirements.title: Associate names remain associated through the block, provide access, and terminate at construct completion
requirements.definition: Each associate name remains associated with its selector throughout the executed block, the selector is known by and accessed by the associate name inside the block, and construct completion terminates the association.
